newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Dealers take 2-3 cts protection.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Dealers take 2-3 cts protection.

text.p: Forecasts for a lower opening in KCBT hard red winter wheat futures Tuesday prompted dealers in the Plains to take two to three cents per bushel protection on hard red winter wheat.
Wheat futures rallied Monday on spillover from gains in CBOT corn and soy, which surged on concern about hot, dry weather in key growing areas of the Midwest.
But the arrival of beneficial rains Monday afternoon in corn- and soy-growing areas of Illinois meant that grains and oilseed futures were being called to open lower Tuesday.
Meanwhile, thick hail and thundershowers were reported Tuesday morning in sections of south central Kansas.
"There were reports of 1-1/2-inch diameter hail toward Kingman County," a Kansas grain dealer said.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
